Sokaogon Chippewa Community

Sokaogon Chippewa Community is a distinct Ojibwe government also known as the Mole Lake Band. Its public history begins with the community's relationship to Rice Lake and manoomin, or wild rice. It recounts Chief Willard Ackley's work to secure a reservation and presents that struggle as part of the community's continued connection to its homeland. The page combines community memory, historical narrative and a recorded voice that was not transcribed in this review. EPA's 2006 water-quality case study provides a second, dated perspective. It describes the community's development of water-quality standards, monitoring and efforts to protect Rice Lake from a proposed upstream mine, including the 2003 land purchase involving Forest County Potawatomi. The official history and agency case study give differing dates and acreage for reservation establishment; this guide leaves that detail unresolved. A community-developed comprehensive plan identifies the pictured Dinesen-Motzfeldt-Hettinger Log House as a historic asset on the reservation. That former trading-post building illustrates one local historical site, not Sokaogon housing generally or the full community story.

Source & image record ↗ · CC BY-SA 3.0

The Community-developed comprehensive plan, printed page 24, explicitly identifies the log house as a historic asset on the reservation and describes its restoration. The photo is a view of that particular former trading-post structure, not generic Ojibwe architecture or a representation of Sokaogon housing. The filename says August 2013 but the record and EXIF specify 1 September 2013; use September. The full building chronology remains outside this image review. 01

Rice Lake in the Community account

The Community's history frames manoomin and Rice Lake as central to local continuity and recalls Chief Ackley's advocacy for a reservation. Exact reservation purchase and recognition chronology remains unresolved across the selected accounts.

Read the sources [1] Sokaogon Chippewa Community

02

Water protection in a dated case study

EPA's 2006 account describes community discussion, water monitoring and the 2003 purchase connected to the proposed Crandon Mine. It documents one stage of Sokaogon's environmental governance, with Forest County Potawatomi as a distinct partner.

Read the sources [2] U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
